memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "You are to be my holy people. So do not eat the meat of an animal torn by wild beasts; throw it to the dogs." - Exodus 22:31 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The chapter closes with a call that gathers up everything before it: "You are to be my holy people." Even something as ordinary as what they ate was to mark Israel out as different, set apart, belonging to God. The specific food law reflected their unique calling, but the heartbeat behind it is timeless: God's people are meant to be distinct, shaped by their belonging to Him in every part of life.

To be holy simply means to be set apart, marked as God's own. It is not about being superior or self-righteous; it is about belonging so fully to God that it shapes how we live, even in small daily choices. The way we speak, spend, work, and treat others is meant to quietly declare, "I belong to Him." Holiness touches the ordinary corners of life, not just the religious moments.

This is who we are in Christ. The New Testament takes up these very words and applies them to all who belong to Jesus: "you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession" (1 Pet 2:9). Holiness is not first a burden to achieve but an identity to live out. You belong to God. Let that beautiful truth shape the way you live today, in the great things and the small.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Does my everyday life quietly declare that I belong to God?
Where is God calling me to live as someone set apart in the ordinary details?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You have made me Your own, set apart to belong to You. Let my whole life — even its small, ordinary details — reflect that I am Yours. Thank You for calling me holy in Christ. Amen.
